research_question: Owned-page scope: Legal Industry Statistics by Firm Size. Planned sources and method: BLS legal-services employment and Census industry receipts; align years. Build a source-labelled comparison covering legal sector employment and law firm revenue; record dates, definitions and sample limits. Sources are proposed, not verified findings.

research_brief.purpose: Show how the U.S. legal industry is structured by firm size, using official counts of firms, employment, and receipts, and separate those from pay and large-firm performance data.
research_brief.audience: Law firm leaders, legal operations and marketing professionals, consultants, journalists, and researchers comparing legal-market figures.
research_brief.data_period: 2022 (Census SUSB, released April 10, 2025); May 2025 (BLS wages); 2025 (Thomson Reuters Institute tracked firms)
research_brief.scope_limitations: Census SUSB covers employer firms in NAICS 541110 and excludes practitioners with no employees. Size is enterprise employment, not lawyer count. Receipts are revenue, not profit. Band totals above nine employees are sums of non-overlapping Census rows; the 500-or-more group is the total minus the under-500 subtotal.

content_gaps: No ranking page shows the Census firm-size distribution for law firms.
No page shows how employment and receipts are split across firm sizes.
Competing pages cite firm counts above 400,000 without explaining that official counts cover employer firms only.
Firm, establishment, and enterprise size are rarely defined.
value_add: Official 2022 Census counts of law firms by size with shares of firms, employment, and receipts calculated from the source rows; clear definitions of firm, establishment, and enterprise size; an explanation of why commercial firm counts are far higher; and separation of structure data from pay and large-firm performance.
